readerTitle: Nine ideas, one quarter: run the planning meeting yourself
caseNote: 가상 시뮬레이션 (동네 국숫집과 자체 온라인 주문 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 분기 목표를 정하는 일은 무엇을 할지보다 무엇을 하지 않을지 정하고, 그 결정을 매주 지키는 일이다.
misconception: 목표는 많고 클수록 좋고, 한 번 정해 두면 분기 말에 결과만 확인하면 된다.

sources.text: 목표 관리의 표준 개념 (목표와 핵심 결과, 운영 리듬, 긴급과 중요의 구분)
Grove, A. (1983). High Output Management. Random House.
모든 수치와 사례는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 점심 손님 60명 → 목표 80명(+33%), 실제 74명(목표 증가분 20명 중 14명, 70% 달성).
앱 재주문율 18% → 목표 30%, 실제 26%(목표 증가분 12%p 중 8%p, 약 67% 달성). 평균 조리·제공 시간 9.5분은 12분 제한 이내.
테이크어웨이 카드의 결정-개념 연결(목표 수 줄이기 = OPS-04-05, 측정 가능한 목표 = OPS-04-02, 주간 점검 = OPS-04-06, 버그 우선 = OPS-04-04)이 각 형제 레슨의 실제 내용과 맞는지 게시 전에 확인하세요.

cards.title: Nine ideas, one quarter, one small restaurant
body: You run a 40-seat neighborhood noodle restaurant. You also have your own online ordering app. Next quarter starts in a week.

Your team's wish list has nine goals: a new menu, catering, scouting a second location, more social posts, a loyalty card, fixing the app, more weekday lunches, less food waste and a staff training plan.
You'll make four calls. Each one shapes the next.

image.label: Restaurant whiteboard crowded with nine sticky notes
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 국숫집 주방 옆 화이트보드에 포스트잇 아홉 장이 빽빽하게 붙어 있고, 앞치마를 두른 사장이 팔짱을 끼고 바라보는 장면. 실제 상호나 로고는 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: Which goals make the cut?
body: Your team is six people plus a freelance app developer who works two days a week. Everyone is already busy running the restaurant.

options.text: Keep all nine. Ambition keeps the team sharp
options.feedback: Each goal gets a sliver of attention. By August most are half done, and nobody can say which ones mattered.

options.text: Pick the two that would change the business most: weekday lunch and repeat app orders
options.feedback: You park seven good ideas for now. In return, every spare hour goes somewhere that counts.

options.text: Pick the four easiest to finish
options.feedback: You'd likely tick boxes. But easy goals are often easy because they don't move much.

cards.title: Say you chose two. Now write the lunch goal.
body: Weekday lunch averages 60 covers (meals served) a day. Nearby office workers leave if food takes too long. Which version goes on the wall?

image.label: A goal card with one aim and two numbers
image.brief: 주방 벽에 붙은 카드 한 장. 위에 큰 글씨로 "Win back weekday lunch", 아래 두 줄 "60 → 80 covers a day", "Food out in under 12 min". 마감일 "by Sep 30"을 작은 달력 아이콘과 함께.

options.text: Become the neighborhood's favorite lunch spot
options.feedback: It inspires, but in week 5 nobody can tell whether it's working.

options.text: Win back weekday lunch: 60 to 80 covers a day by September 30, with food out in under 12 minutes
options.feedback: A clear aim plus numbers that show progress. The time limit stops you from chasing covers with a line out the door.
Measurable, but with no target or deadline. A 2% rise would count as success.

cards.title: Say you wrote the 80-cover goal. How will you watch it?
body: The goal is on the wall. Now it has to survive twelve busy weeks of service, deliveries and staff schedules.

options.text: Check total revenue at the end of each month
options.feedback: You'll see trouble, but weeks late. And revenue mixes lunch with dinner and app orders.

options.text: Post daily covers and food times, and review them every Monday in a 15-minute huddle
options.feedback: It costs 15 minutes a week. You spot a slow week fast enough to try a fix before the next one.

options.text: Trust the team and check at the end of September
options.feedback: No meetings at all. But you learn the result only when it's too late to change anything.

cards.title: Say you chose the Monday huddle. Week 6, an urgent request lands.
body: Your app goal: raise the share of app customers who order again within 30 days from 18% to 30%. Your developer just found a checkout bug that logs some returning users out.
Then a large office nearby asks for a catering page in the app "within two weeks." Your developer has time for one.

options.text: Build the catering page. A big client is asking now
options.feedback: You might win the client. But the bug keeps pushing returning users away, and the app goal stalls for the rest of the quarter.

options.text: Fix the bug. Take the office's catering orders by email for now, and put the page on next quarter's list
options.feedback: The client gets a plainer process but still gets fed. Your developer's two days stay on the goal you chose.

options.text: Ask the developer to split time between both
options.feedback: It sounds fair. Often both arrive late and neither is done well.

cards.title: You missed both targets and had your best quarter in two years.
body: Two goals, watched every week, moved further than nine goals ever had.

breakdown.label: Weekday lunch covers a day
breakdown.detail: Goal was 80. A Monday huddle caught a slow week 4, and a faster set lunch fixed it.

breakdown.label: App customers reordering within 30 days
breakdown.detail: Goal was 30%. The week-7 bug fix did most of the work.

breakdown.label: Ideas parked
breakdown.detail: The catering page is first on next quarter's list

cards.title: A number can be hit the wrong way.
body: You could reach 80 covers with a half-price lunch coupon. The goal would turn green while profit falls. Pair each target with a **guard number**, like serving time or profit per meal, that must not get worse.
And a stretch goal you nearly hit isn't a failure. If people are punished for missing, next quarter they'll quietly set goals they know they can beat.

image.label: A green goal light next to a falling profit arrow
image.brief: 계기판 스타일 일러스트. 왼쪽에 "80 covers" 초록불이 켜져 있고, 오른쪽에 "Profit per meal" 화살표가 아래로 떨어짐. 바닥에 반값 쿠폰이 흩어져 있음. 로고 없음.

cards.title: Fewer goals, sharper numbers, a weekly look, a firm no.
body: Each call you made is one idea from this unit.
list: **Two goals, not nine:** the cost of doing too much
**An aim with numbers and a date:** objectives and key results
**The bug before the catering page:** urgent vs important
cards.callout: **Try it today:** write your goals for next quarter. Cut the list to two, give each a number and a date, and pick the day each week you'll look at them.
